title: Trump Returns to US After Historic Two-Day Beijing Summit — China Disputes 'Fantastic Trade Deals' Claims; Taiwan Arms Sale Held as 'Negotiating Chip'
detail: President Trump departed Beijing on May 15, 2026, concluding a two-day state visit — the first US presidential visit to China since Trump's own 2017 trip. Trump visited Zhongnanhai before boarding Air Force One, stopping in Anchorage before landing at Joint Base Andrews ~6:30 p.m. EDT. On the flight home, Trump claimed 'fantastic trade deals' including a Chinese commitment to buy 200 Boeing aircraft, increased US crude oil purchases, and agricultural goods in the 'double-digit billions.' However, Chinese officials did not confirm these specific commitments, and analysts noted no formal breakthrough agreements were signed — both governments publicly disagreed on what was agreed. The main verified outcomes were: both leaders agreed the Strait of Hormuz 'must remain open'; Xi warned on Taiwan; Trump invited Xi to the White House September 24; and a 'strategic stability' framework was set as the governing framework. On Air Force One, Trump said he was 'undecided' on whether to approve a planned $14 billion arms sale to Taiwan, calling it 'a very good negotiating chip for us.'

media.caption: Trump wraps up two-day China trip; invites Xi for September White House visit

title: House Fails to Advance Iran War Powers Resolution on 212-212 Tied Vote — Third Consecutive Democratic Defeat
detail: The House of Representatives failed to advance an Iran war powers resolution on May 15, 2026, with the vote ending in a 212-212 tie — the third consecutive failed Democratic attempt to rein in Trump's authority to conduct military operations against Iran. Under the War Powers Resolution, a 60-day clock for unauthorized troop engagement had already passed without congressional action; the Trump administration argues the ceasefire pauses the WPR clock, a legal position Democrats dispute. The tied vote underscored the inability of House Democrats — without Republican crossover support — to force a binding war powers vote during an ongoing fragile ceasefire with Iran.

media.caption: House Iran war powers vote fails 212-212 — third consecutive Democratic defeat

title: Trump Says He'd Accept 20-Year Iran Nuclear Enrichment Suspension — Signals Diplomatic Off-Ramp
detail: President Trump stated on May 15, 2026, that he would accept Iran suspending nuclear enrichment for 20 years if there is a 'real' guarantee and commitment — signaling a potential diplomatic off-ramp from the ongoing US-Iran conflict. The statement represented a significant softening from earlier US demands for permanent nuclear dismantlement, and came as the fragile ceasefire continued to hold despite tensions. Iran had not issued a formal response to the latest US diplomatic framework. The 20-year suspension window aligns with frameworks proposed during prior nuclear negotiations and could form the basis of a 'Hormuz first, nuclear later' deal structure that US intermediaries have discussed. Pakistan and Qatar remain active as mediation channels.

media.caption: Trump says he'd accept Iran suspending nuclear program for 20 years with real commitment

title: Trump Misses Legal Deadline to Disclose Tens of Millions in Stock Trades — Washington Post
detail: President Trump missed a legal deadline on May 15, 2026 to disclose tens of millions of dollars in stock trades, according to a Washington Post report. Presidents are required by law to disclose financial transactions; the missed deadline raised questions about compliance with federal ethics disclosure requirements. The disclosure issue comes as Trump's personal finances have been a recurring point of controversy, and as Democrats were already highlighting an IRS settlement controversy (a purported settlement with the IRS over Trump's previously filed $10 billion lawsuit) as evidence of executive self-dealing.

media.caption: Trump misses legal deadline to disclose tens of millions in stock trades
